content.text: Demos in the peer repository are standalone; only tests include libraries, via the runner's combined-file mechanism. I'll mirror that mechanism in the demo runner and document the rule.

input.command:
cat > scripts/run-mlpl-demo <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Run a demo that includes repository libraries.
#
# `include` resolves relative to the INCLUDING file, and `--source-dir` only
# bounds the sandbox, so a script under demos/ cannot reach lib/. The test
# runner solves this by concatenating sources into one file; this script does
# the same: every `include "path"` line in the demo is replaced, in order, by
# the contents of that path, and the combined program runs from a temp file.
set -eu

[ "$#" -ge 1 ] || { echo "usage: run-mlpl-demo <demo.mlpl> [interpreter args...]" >&2; exit 2; }

repo_root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
mlpl=$("$repo_root/scripts/select-mlpl")
demo=$1
shift

tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() { rm -rf -- "$tmp_dir"; }
trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM
combined="$tmp_dir/combined.mlpl"

: > "$combined"
seen=""
while IFS= read -r line; do
    case "$line" in
        include\ \"*\"*)
            path=$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/^include *"\([^"]*\)".*$/\1/')
            case " $seen " in
                *" $path "*) continue ;;
            esac
            [ -f "$repo_root/$path" ] || { echo "included source missing: $path" >&2; exit 1; }
            seen="$seen $path"
            printf '# --- included: %s\n' "$path" >> "$combined"
            cat "$repo_root/$path" >> "$combined"
            printf '\n' >> "$combined"
            ;;
        *)
            printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$combined"
            ;;
    esac
done < "$repo_root/$demo"

exec "$mlpl" --source-dir "$repo_root" --data-dir "$repo_root" "$@" -f "$combined"
EOF
chmod +x scripts/run-mlpl-demo && python3 - <<'PY'
p='scripts/run-math500-self-grade'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('exec "$mlpl" --source-dir "$repo_root" "$repo_root/demos/math500_self_grade.mlpl"','exec "$repo_root/scripts/run-mlpl-demo" demos/math500_self_grade.mlpl')
s=s.replace('mlpl=$("$repo_root/scripts/select-mlpl")\n','')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
sh -n scripts/run-mlpl-demo scripts/run-math500-self-grade && ./scripts/run-math500-self-grade 2>&1 | tail -10

demo-coding-agent/docs/mlplcode.org
#+title: mlplcode, a coding agent in sw-MLPL
#+subtitle: a literate reading of every MLPL file in the agent
#+author: Michael A Wright
#+startup: showall
#+property: header-args:mlpl :results output :exports code :eval no-export
#+property: header-args:text :eval never
#+property: header-args:emacs-lisp :eval no-export
#+options: toc:2 num:t

* How to read and run this document

This is the agent, in the order a reader should meet it, with prose before
every function. Each source block carries a ~:tangle~ target: tangling this
file regenerates the committed sources byte for byte, and ~just check~ runs
~scripts/check-tangle~ to prove it, so the prose can never describe code that
no longer exists. The committed ~.mlpl~ files remain the source of truth;
when they change, this document is edited to match.

** Evaluating blocks

The document never evaluates anything on export (~:eval no-export~ in the
header), so =C-c C-e h o= produces HTML with no prompts. Evaluation is for
reading interactively. To make =C-c C-c= work, evaluate this setup block
once per Emacs session; it loads sw-MLPL's org-babel backend from the
adjacent checkout and points it at whichever interpreter exists (GUI Emacs
has a minimal PATH, so the full path matters):

#+begin_src emacs-lisp :tangle no
(let* ((here (file-name-directory (buffer-file-name)))
       ;; The repository root is wherever AGENTS.md is, so this also works
       ;; on a copy of the document under out/ or work/.
       (repo (or (locate-dominating-file here "AGENTS.md") (expand-file-name ".." here)))
       (sw-mlpl (expand-file-name "../sw-mlpl" repo))
       (candidates (list (expand-file-name "target/release/mlpl-repl" sw-mlpl)
                         (expand-file-name "target/debug/mlpl-repl" sw-mlpl)
                         (executable-find "mlpl-repl")
                         (expand-file-name "~/.local/softwarewrighter/bin/mlpl-repl"))))
  (add-to-list 'load-path (expand-file-name "elisp" sw-mlpl))
  (require 'ob-mlpl)
  ;; Keep org-babel's scratch files inside the repository's ignored work/
  ;; directory rather than /tmp.
  (make-directory (expand-file-name "work" repo) t)
  (setq temporary-file-directory (expand-file-name "work/" repo))
  (setq org-babel-mlpl-command
        (or (seq-find (lambda (p) (and p (file-executable-p p))) candidates)
            (user-error "no mlpl-repl found; build ../sw-mlpl or set org-babel-mlpl-command")))
  (setq org-confirm-babel-evaluate nil)
  (message "ob-mlpl ready: %s" org-babel-mlpl-command))
#+end_src

Three things to know before pressing =C-c C-c= on a block:

- A block runs in a fresh interpreter on a temporary file, so a block that
  says ~include "model.mlpl"~ cannot find its neighbour and will report an
  include error. The function blocks in this document are for reading and
  tangling; the runnable ones are the small self-contained examples in the
  primer below.
- ~org-confirm-babel-evaluate~ controls the yes/no prompt. The setup block
  sets it to ~nil~ (never ask) for the session; set it back to ~t~ to be
  asked, or to a function to decide per block.
=== ob-mlpl naming ===
mlpl-all.el
mlpl-bootstrap.el
mlpl-fold.el
mlpl-init-example.el
mlpl-menu.el
mlpl-mode.el
mlpl-org.el
mlpl-repl.el
mlpl-svg.el
mlpl.el
ob-mlpl.el

sw-mlpl/elisp/mlpl-all.el:40:  (require 'ob-mlpl)   ; provides org-babel-execute:mlpl
sw-mlpl/elisp/mlpl-all.el:52:           (featurep 'ob-mlpl) (featurep 'mlpl-org)))

content.text:
The verifier is complete and committed. Saga 1 now has nine steps, seven done.

**What landed this step.** Three modules and two test suites, 37 tests passing:

- `lib/verify/number.mlpl`: exact rational arithmetic with a floating fallback only where mathematics forces it, plus perfect-square detection and an exact-integer limit.
- `lib/verify/expr.mlpl`: a bounded recursive-descent parser with correct precedence, right-associative exponents, unary signs binding looser than powers, implicit multiplication, `sqrt`, `pi`, `e`, and failures classified as budget, syntax, or symbolic.
- `lib/verify/grade.mlpl`: top-level tuple splitting, ordered part-wise comparison, totality on malformed input, and the reward function reinforcement learning will call.

**The divergence I had predicted did not happen.** Parsing decimals as exact rationals rather than floats makes `0.5` equal `1/2` while `0.3333333333` stays unequal to `1/3`, matching the reference exactly. The only remaining difference is symbolic rearrangement, which the tests pin deliberately.

**Real validation.** `just math500-self-grade` downloads the 500-problem set and grades every reference answer against itself: 500 of 500 correct, zero false positives, 15.7 seconds. That is the reference suite's own criterion.

**One repository-shaping discovery.** `include` resolves relative to the including file and `--source-dir` only bounds the sandbox, so a script under `demos/` cannot reach `lib/`. Tests work because the test runner concatenates sources. I added `scripts/run-mlpl-demo`, which inlines includes the same way, and wrote the rule into `AGENTS.md`.

**On your org-mode question**: it is `ob-mlpl`, with `#+begin_src mlpl` blocks. I queued it as step 9, modeled on `demo-coding-agent/docs/mlplcode.org`: prose before every block, `:tangle` targets that regenerate the committed sources byte for byte, a `scripts/check-tangle` comparison wired into `just check`, and runnable self-contained examples. Keeping it current is now a cross-cutting rule in the plan, so the document can never describe code that no longer exists.

**Upstream**: four of nine core requests shipped today, all probe-verified. The tokenizer extension and the remaining libraries are queued in their repositories; nothing blocks the next two steps.

content.text:
Step 8 is committed; Saga 1 has one step left. Here is the status you asked for.

**Upstream requests: 5 of 9 core items shipped, all today, each verified by a probe.**

| Request | Status |
|---|---|
| R1 `sqrt` backward | shipped 0dfa3eae |
| R1 `pow` (constant integer exponent) | shipped 8a1fe24a |
| R5 `sin`/`cos` backward | shipped 0dfa3eae |
| R6 scientific-notation literals | shipped 2a774891 |
| R3 rank-3 `matmul` actionable error | shipped fdb5e675 (the error half; batched matmul itself still pending) |
| R2 axis `softmax` on the tape | pending |
| R3 batched `matmul` | pending |
| R4 `transpose_axes` backward | pending |
| R7 `bf16`/`f16` dtype | pending |
| R9 MLX build and dispatch | pending |

Plus one fix I never filed: lenient string escapes for LaTeX text (3250cea9), which removed a lexer limitation I had worked around.

**Sibling repositories are delivering too.** `demo-mlpl-libraries` has shipped two of five requested libraries: text helpers and a bounded JSON Lines reader. `demo-extensions` has completed the first step of the large-download core, with the tokenizer extension next in its queue.

**Yes, we are making progress.** Saga 1 is eight of nine steps done. Every request has a probe, so when a fix lands the gate reports drift and the ledger gets corrected deliberately rather than silently.

**What you can demo right now.** All of it runs with no model and no network:

- `just verifier-demo` walks a three-stage narrated pipeline: extraction, normalization and evaluation of five answer forms; seven grading pairs showing why `0.5` equals one half but a truncated `0.3333333333` does not equal one third; then a stand-in responder evaluated over the fixture, scoring 3 of 5 under the strict boxed rule and 4 of 5 with the numeric fallback, which is exactly the difference between a reward signal and a base-model measurement.
- `just math500-self-grade` grades all 500 real reference answers against themselves: 500 of 500 correct, zero false positives, 15.7 seconds.
- `just capabilities` prints the live capability ledger against the current interpreter build.
- `just check` runs 45 tests, the probes, and the demo.

**What you can demo soon.** The literate org-mode document is next, one step away: a readable `docs/reasoning.org` you can export or evaluate block by block with `ob-mlpl`, whose tangled output must match the committed sources byte for byte. After that, Saga 2 gives a tokenizer demo, and Saga 3 gives the first actual text generation, though that one waits on real-model throughput.

**What is still gated.** Only three things need upstream work: the tokenizer extension for production-speed encoding, and the MLX build plus batched matmul for real-model inference and training. Nothing blocks the next two sagas' development work.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

# Gate check: docs/mlplcode.org must reproduce every source it explains.
# Tangle rule (the same one org-babel-tangle applies): for each
# `#+begin_src <lang> :tangle <path>` block, in document order, the block
# body is appended to <path> (relative to docs/) with one blank line between
# blocks. Implemented in awk so the check needs no Emacs; when Emacs is
# available the same tangle is also run through org-babel-tangle and must
# agree.
repo_dir=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
org=$repo_dir/docs/mlplcode.org
# Scratch lives under the ignored ./work directory, never /tmp.
work=$repo_dir/work/tangle-awk.$$
rm -rf "$work"; mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

awk -v out="$work" '
/^#\+begin_src / {
    target = ""
    for (i = 2; i <= NF; i++) if ($i == ":tangle") target = $(i + 1)
    if (target != "" && target != "no") {
        sub(/^\.\.\//, "", target)
        file = out "/" target
        dir = file; sub(/\/[^\/]*$/, "", dir)
        system("mkdir -p \"" dir "\"")
        if (file in seen) printf "\n" >> file
        seen[file] = 1
        inblock = 1
        next
    }
}
/^#\+end_src/ { inblock = 0; next }
inblock { print >> file }
' "$org"

status=0
count=0
for tangled in $(cd "$work" && find . -type f | sort); do
    rel=${tangled#./}
    count=$((count + 1))
    if ! cmp -s "$work/$rel" "$repo_dir/$rel"; then
        echo "tangle drift: docs/mlplcode.org does not reproduce $rel" >&2
        diff "$repo_dir/$rel" "$work/$rel" | head -20 >&2
        status=1
    fi
done
[ "$count" -gt 0 ] || { echo "no tangle targets found in docs/mlplcode.org" >&2; exit 1; }

emacs=${EMACS:-}

This is the first half of a from-scratch reasoning model: everything needed to

next-token predictor into a model that reasons, and the mechanism for that is
reinforcement learning from a *verifiable reward*. The reward is exactly the

Three self-contained blocks, each complete enough to run on its own.

The first shows why normalization exists. Two answers that share almost no
characters denote the same number:

The second shows the exact-rational decision that the verifier turns on. A
decimal is a rational, so a half is a half, but a truncated third is not a

#+startup: showall

* How to read and run this document

This is the first half of a from-scratch reasoning model: everything needed to
*decide whether an answer is right*, written in sw-MLPL, with prose before
every block. It is a literate reading of the committed sources, not a
paraphrase of them. Each source block carries a =:tangle= target, and
=scripts/check-tangle= runs in the pre-commit gate to prove that tangling this
document reproduces every file it explains, byte for byte. The =.mlpl= files
remain the source of truth; when they change, this document is edited to
match, and the gate fails until it is.

Why a verifier comes before a model: the project's goal is to turn a plain
next-token predictor into a model that reasons, and the mechanism for that is
reinforcement learning from a *verifiable reward*. The reward is exactly the
function in this document. There is no reward model and no human labels; a
rollout scores one if its boxed answer verifies against the reference and zero
otherwise. Building the reward first means every later claim about accuracy is
measurable from the start. The full picture is in
[[file:how-base-becomes-reasoning.md][how-base-becomes-reasoning.md]].

The document never evaluates anything on export (=:eval no-export= in the
header), so exporting produces no prompts. Evaluation is for reading
interactively. To make =C-c C-c= work, evaluate this setup block once per
Emacs session; it loads sw-MLPL's Org-babel backend from the adjacent checkout
and points it at whichever interpreter exists:

  (add-to-list 'load-path (expand-file-name "elisp" sw-mlpl))

Two things to know before pressing =C-c C-c=:

- A block runs in a fresh interpreter on a temporary file, so a block that
  says =include "lib/text/text.mlpl"= cannot find its neighbour. This is not a
  quirk of Org: =include= resolves relative to the including file and

Three self-contained blocks, each complete enough to run on its own.

The first shows why normalization exists. Two answers that share almost no
characters denote the same number:

#+begin_src mlpl :tangle no
print("dfrac and a plain fraction look nothing alike:")

decimal is a rational, so a half is a half, but a truncated third is not a

print("0.5 equals 1/2 exactly:       ", eq(0.5, half))

cat > scripts/check-tangle <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

# Gate check: docs/reasoning.org must reproduce every source it explains.
# Tangle rule (the same one org-babel-tangle applies): for each
# `#+begin_src <lang> :tangle <path>` block, in document order, the block body
# is appended to <path> (relative to docs/) with one blank line between
# blocks. Implemented in awk so the check needs no Emacs; when Emacs is
# available the same tangle also runs through org-babel-tangle and must agree.
repo_dir=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
org=$repo_dir/docs/reasoning.org
work=$repo_dir/out/tangle-awk.$$
rm -rf "$work"; mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

awk -v out="$work" '
/^#\+begin_src / {
    target = ""
    for (i = 2; i <= NF; i++) if ($i == ":tangle") target = $(i + 1)
    if (target != "" && target != "no") {
        sub(/^\.\.\//, "", target)
        file = out "/" target
        dir = file; sub(/\/[^\/]*$/, "", dir)
        system("mkdir -p \"" dir "\"")
        if (file in seen) printf "\n" >> file
        seen[file] = 1
        inblock = 1
        next
    }
}
/^#\+end_src/ { inblock = 0; next }
inblock { print >> file }
' "$org"

status=0
count=0
for tangled in $(cd "$work" && find . -type f | sort); do
    rel=${tangled#./}
    count=$((count + 1))
    if ! cmp -s "$work/$rel" "$repo_dir/$rel"; then
        echo "tangle drift: docs/reasoning.org does not reproduce $rel" >&2
        diff "$repo_dir/$rel" "$work/$rel" | head -20 >&2
        status=1
    fi
done
[ "$count" -gt 0 ] || { echo "no tangle targets found in docs/reasoning.org" >&2; exit 1; }

# Every library the document claims to explain must actually be tangled.
for source in $(cd "$repo_dir" && find lib -name '*.mlpl' | sort); do
    [ -f "$work/$source" ] || {
        echo "docs/reasoning.org does not explain $source" >&2
        status=1
    }
done

emacs=${EMACS:-$(command -v emacs 2>/dev/null || true)}
if [ -n "$emacs" ] && [ -x "$emacs" ]; then
    emacs_work=$repo_dir/out/tangle-emacs.$$
    rm -rf "$emacs_work"; mkdir -p "$emacs_work/docs"
    cp "$org" "$emacs_work/docs/reasoning.org"
    "$emacs" --batch --eval "(progn (require 'org) (find-file \"$emacs_work/docs/reasoning.org\") (org-babel-tangle))" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    for tangled in $(cd "$work" && find . -type f | sort); do
        rel=${tangled#./}
        if [ -f "$emacs_work/$rel" ] && ! cmp -s "$emacs_work/$rel" "$work/$rel"; then
            echo "tangle disagreement between org-babel-tangle and the awk rule for $rel" >&2
            status=1
        fi
    done
    rm -rf "$emacs_work"
    echo "tangle: $count file(s) reproduced (awk and org-babel-tangle agree)"
else
    echo "tangle: $count file(s) reproduced (awk rule; Emacs not present)"
fi

exit "$status"
EOF
chmod +x scripts/check-tangle && ./scripts/check-tangle; echo "exit=$?"

+# `#+begin_src <lang> :tangle <path>` block, in document order, the block body
+# is appended to <path> (relative to docs/) with one blank line between
+# blocks. Implemented in awk so the check needs no Emacs; when Emacs is
+# available the same tangle also runs through org-babel-tangle and must agree.
+    for (i = 2; i <= NF; i++) if ($i == ":tangle") target = $(i + 1)
+for tangled in $(cd "$work" && find . -type f | sort); do
+        echo "tangle drift: docs/reasoning.org does not reproduce $rel" >&2
+[ "$count" -gt 0 ] || { echo "no tangle targets found in docs/reasoning.org" >&2; exit 1; }
+# Every library the document claims to explain must actually be tangled.
+for source in $(cd "$repo_dir" && find lib -name '*.mlpl' | sort); do
+    for tangled in $(cd "$work" && find . -type f | sort); do
+            echo "tangle disagreement between org-babel-tangle and the awk rule for $rel" >&2
+    echo "tangle: $count file(s) reproduced (awk and org-babel-tangle agree)"
+    echo "tangle: $count file(s) reproduced (awk rule; Emacs not present)"

content.text:
**Saga 1 is complete.** Nine steps, all committed on `main`, gate passing.

**The literate document is in.** `docs/reasoning.org` is a reading of the entire verifier and harness for `ob-mlpl`: prose before each of 52 source blocks, a setup block that finds your interpreter, a five-minute primer with three self-contained runnable examples, and tangle targets covering all eight library files. `scripts/check-tangle` implements the tangle rule in awk, reproduces every source byte for byte, cross-checks against `org-babel-tangle` when Emacs is present, and fails if any library is not explained. It runs in `just check`, so the prose can never describe code that no longer exists.

I verified the three primer blocks actually execute and print what the surrounding prose claims, including the exact-rational demonstration that a truncated third differs from one third by 3.3e-11.

**The drift detector earned its keep again.** Mid-step, `just check` failed because upstream shipped axis-aware softmax on the tape (build 363391a6, request R2). I reconciled the probe, ledger, and request document before closing.

**Upstream tally now: 5 of 9 core requests fully shipped, 1 half-shipped**, all today. Shipped: `sqrt`, `pow`, `sin`/`cos`, scientific literals, axis softmax. Half: rank-3 `matmul` has an actionable error, the batched operation is still open. Pending: `transpose_axes` backward, `bf16` dtype, MLX build. Siblings have delivered two of five libraries; the tokenizer extension is still absent.

**What you can demo right now**, all offline and fast:

- `just verifier-demo` narrates the pipeline and shows the strict-versus-fallback scoring difference.
- `just math500-self-grade` grades all 500 real reference answers: 500 correct, 0 false positives.
- `just tangle` proves the literate document reproduces every source.
- `just capabilities` prints the live ledger.
- Open `docs/reasoning.org` in Emacs, evaluate the setup block, and press `C-c C-c` on any primer block.

**Next** is Saga 2, the tokenizer: parse a real `tokenizer.json`, write the MLPL reference byte-level encoder on a synthetic fixture, and build the chat templates. Only its final parity-and-throughput step waits on the extension.

Measure and record parse time and peak memory on the real 7 MB file in docs/sw-mlpl-blockers.md (it is currently in the not-yet-measured section). EOF

Keep it readable: this is the oracle the Rust extension is checked against, not the production path. Write tests/test_tokenizer_bpe.mlpl against the synthetic fixture only: byte mapping round-trip, pre-tokenization boundaries, merge ordering including a tie, single-character and empty input, and the expected id sequences from fixtures/tokenizer/tiny-expected.jsonl. Record encode throughput on a few hundred characters so the later extension comparison has a baseline. Update the catalog, docs/reasoning.org, README, and docs/sagas.md.
EOF
cat > $S/steps/t3.md <<'EOF'

Write tests/test_tokenizer_template.mlpl covering round-trip decode on the fixture, control-token splitting, both template variants, and the end-of-sequence rule per model kind. Update the catalog, docs/reasoning.org, README, and docs/sagas.md.
EOF

cat > scripts/fetch-model <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Download the Qwen3-0.6B-Base tokenizer and config into the ignored models/
# tree. Opt-in: never part of `just check`. Prints provenance, checks the
# published byte sizes, and refuses to overwrite existing files.
#
# The weights themselves (model.safetensors, 1,192,135,096 bytes) are a
# separate, much larger download added by the saga step that needs them.
set -eu

repo_root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
base="https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base/resolve/main"
dest_dir="$repo_root/models/qwen3-0.6b-base"

echo "Qwen3-0.6B-Base tokenizer and configuration"
echo "  source:  $base"
echo "  license: Apache-2.0 (see the model card)"
echo "  dest:    models/qwen3-0.6b-base/ (ignored by git, never redistributed)"

fetch() {
    name=$1
    expected=$2
    target="$dest_dir/$name"
    if [ -e "$target" ]; then
        echo "  skip:    $name already present" >&2
        return 0
    fi
    mkdir -p "$dest_dir"
    tmp="$target.part"
    curl -L --fail --silent --show-error -o "$tmp" "$base/$name"
    actual=$(wc -c < "$tmp" | tr -d ' ')
    if [ "$expected" -gt 0 ] && [ "$actual" -ne "$expected" ]; then
        rm -f "$tmp"
        echo "size mismatch for $name: expected $expected bytes, got $actual" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    mv "$tmp" "$target"
    echo "  bytes:   $name $actual"
}

fetch tokenizer.json 7031645
fetch config.json 0
EOF
chmod +x scripts/fetch-model && perl -0pi -e 's/# Download the MATH-500 evaluation set/# Download the Qwen3-0.6B-Base tokenizer and config (opt-in, not in check).\nfetch-model:\n    .\/scripts\/fetch-model\n\n# Download the MATH-500 evaluation set/' justfile && sh -n scripts/fetch-model && ./scripts/fetch-model && ls -la models/qwen3-0.6b-base/ && python3 -c "
import json
d=json.load(open('models/qwen3-0.6b-base/tokenizer.json'))
print('top keys:', list(d.keys()))
print('model type:', d['model']['type'])
print('vocab size:', len(d['model']['vocab']), 'merges:', len(d['model']['merges']))
print('merge sample:', d['model']['merges'][:3], type(d['model']['merges'][0]))
print('added tokens:', len(d['added_tokens']), [t['content'] for t in d['added_tokens'][:4]])
print('pre_tokenizer type:', d['pre_tokenizer']['type'])
print('decoder type:', d['decoder']['type'])
print('model keys:', list(d['model'].keys()))
"
